what_its_for: Divalproex is used to treat seizures (epilepsy), bipolar disorder (manic episodes), and to prevent migraine headaches. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other conditions not listed here.
how_to_take: Take divalproex exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. If you are using the Sprinkle capsules, you can open them and sprinkle the contents onto a small amount of soft food like applesauce, then swallow right away without chewing. Do not store the food mixture for later use.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your condition, weight, and how you respond to the medicine. Most adults start at a low dose and the doctor will slowly increase it. Take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Do not change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause serious problems.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store divalproex at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that is expired — check the label and safely dispose of old medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking divalproex, as it can increase drowsiness and the risk of side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines — including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements — without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as many medicines can interact with divalproex. Tell your doctor if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant, as this medicine can cause serious birth defects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting (signs of liver or pancreas problems), unusual bleeding or bruising, thoughts of suicide or hurting yourself, sudden mood changes or worsening depression, rash or blisters on your skin, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, loss of appetite with extreme tiredness, or significant hair loss. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, or if your seizures get worse.
when_it_works: It may take several days to a few weeks before you feel the full benefit of divalproex. For seizures, some improvement may be noticed within the first few days. For bipolar disorder, mood stabilization may take 1 to 2 weeks or longer. For migraine prevention, it may take several weeks of regular use. Do not stop taking the medicine if you do not feel better right away — talk to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Divalproex can cause serious birth defects, especially neural tube defects (problems with the baby's brain and spine), and is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Talk to your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Children: Divalproex is approved for use in children for seizures and migraines, but children under 2 years old have a higher risk of serious liver problems. Older adults (65+): Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially drowsiness and falls. Liver or kidney disease: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as the dose may need to be adjusted or this medicine may not be safe for you.
